title: Far as Thy Name Is Known
description: Far as Thy Name Is Known in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 48, part 2, headed “The beauty of the church; or, Gospel worship and order”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Far as thy name is known The world de-clares thy praise; Thy saints, O Lord, be-fore thy throne Their songs of hon-our raise.

lines: Far as thy name is known
Thy saints, O Lord, before thy throne
Proclaim the wonders of thy hand,
Compass and view thine holy ground,
The cheerful songs, the solemn vows;
Beyond the pomp that charms the eyes,
Will guide us till we die,
Will be our God while here below,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
